seo.title: Pepper Farm Tour in Kampot (2026) | tabiji.ai
seo.metaDescription: Discover the best pepper farm tour in Kampot for 2026 — curated picks with maps, hours, and insider tips.

hero.h1: Tour a riverside pepper plantation to taste the world-famous Kampot pepper — black, red, white, and green — straight from the vine in Cambodia.
hero.subtitle: Immerse yourself in the aromatic world of Kampot pepper with guided tours and tastings at Cambodia's renowned riverside plantations.

picks.name: La Plantation
picks.whyItMadeTheList: La Plantation is arguably the most famous and comprehensive pepper farm, offering free guided tours in multiple languages. Its vast estate boasts stunning views, an onsite restaurant serving pepper-infused dishes, and a shop with a wide range of Kampot pepper products. It's an ideal stop for a full day's exploration.
picks.whatToOrder: Pepper tasting flight, followed by the Lok Lak with Kampot Pepper in their restaurant.
picks.insiderTip: Allocate at least 2-3 hours to fully enjoy the tour, tasting, and a meal. They offer free pickup from certain locations – check their website or ask your guesthouse.
picks.redditQuote: "La Plantation is a must-do in Kampot! The tour was super informative, and honestly, their restaurant had some of the best food we ate in Cambodia, especially the fresh pepper dishes. Don't skip the tasting!"

picks.name: BoTree Farm
picks.whyItMadeTheList: BoTree Farm is renowned for its commitment to organic farming and high-quality pepper. The tours here are intimate and focus deeply on the cultivation process, from vine to spice. Visitors appreciate the detailed explanations and the chance to taste genuinely organic Kampot pepper.
picks.whatToOrder: Organic Black Kampot Pepper (to take home) and a fresh pepper salad if available.
picks.insiderTip: They also produce high-quality salt. Ask for a combined tasting if you're interested in understanding the local salt industry too.
picks.redditQuote: "BoTree Farm gave us such an in-depth look at organic pepper farming. The guides were passionate, and you could really taste the difference in their organic pepper compared to others. Worth the drive!"

picks.name: Farmlink / Kampot Pepper Farm
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Farmlink is known for its strong focus on fair trade practices, directly benefiting local farmers. Their tours provide excellent insights into the entire pepper production cycle and emphasize the importance of sustainable agriculture. It's a great choice for travelers keen on supporting ethical tourism.
picks.whatToOrder: Buy a selection of their fair-trade pepper, particularly the red variety for its unique sweetness.
picks.insiderTip: They often have smaller tour groups, which allows for more personalized questions and interactions with the guides.
picks.redditQuote: "Visited Farmlink and was really impressed by their commitment to fair trade. The tour was educational, and it felt good knowing my purchase directly supported the farmers. Plus, the pepper is amazing."

picks.name: Sothy's Pepper Farm
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Sothy's Pepper Farm offers a more intimate and budget-friendly experience, often praised for its welcoming family atmosphere. The tours are typically led by a family member, providing a personal touch and insights into local life beyond just pepper farming. It's a charming, unpretentious visit.
picks.whatToOrder: Try their fried rice with fresh green Kampot pepper – a local delicacy often available.
picks.insiderTip: Combine your visit with a trip to nearby Kep for a fresh crab lunch, as Sothy's is conveniently located between Kampot town and Kep.
picks.redditQuote: "Sothy's was a really sweet, authentic experience. The family was so welcoming, and the tour was simple but informative. It felt less touristy than some of the bigger farms, which I loved."

picks.name: Starling Farm (Gourmet Kampot Pepper)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Starling Farm focuses on producing gourmet-grade Kampot pepper, often supplying high-end restaurants worldwide. Their tours highlight the meticulous care and traditional methods used to cultivate this premium spice. It's an excellent choice for serious foodies and those interested in the nuances of pepper quality.
picks.whatToOrder: Their gourmet tasting set, showcasing the different pepper varieties and their unique flavor profiles.
picks.insiderTip: Check if they offer any cooking demonstrations or workshops, as they sometimes have special events focused on using their premium pepper.
picks.redditQuote: "If you're serious about your spices, Starling Farm is the place. Their tour went deep into the quality control and processes. The pepper tasted incredible, totally worth the price."

picks.name: Samon's Pepper Farm
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Samon's Pepper Farm offers visitors a direct and engaging tour led by Samon himself or a family member. The focus is on the personal story of their farm, the challenges and rewards of growing Kampot pepper, and an authentic tasting experience. It's highly recommended for a genuine local interaction.
picks.whatToOrder: Any of their freshly dried Kampot pepper, knowing you're supporting a local family directly.
picks.insiderTip: The best way to get here is by tuk-tuk or scooter. Ask your driver to wait as it's a bit off the main road.
picks.redditQuote: "Samon's was such a personal experience. Samon explained everything with so much passion, and you could tell he genuinely loves his farm. Felt good buying direct from him."

picks.name: Fish Island Pepper Farm
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Located on the picturesque Fish Island, this farm offers a unique tour experience. Getting there involves crossing a bridge to the island, making the journey part of the adventure. The tour focuses on the cultivation in this distinct riverside environment, followed by a tasting of their flavorful pepper.
picks.whatToOrder: Any pepper product from their shop; the scenic ride to the farm is a highlight itself.
picks.insiderTip: Rent a scooter to explore Fish Island fully after your farm visit; there are other interesting spots and local life to observe.
picks.redditQuote: "Going to Fish Island Pepper Farm was an adventure! The ride across the bridge and through the villages was half the fun. The farm itself was lovely, and the pepper tasted fantastic."

picks.name: Secret Garden Pepper Farm
picks.whyItMadeTheList: True to its name, this farm offers a slightly more secluded and relaxed experience. It’s a smaller operation but provides an intimate understanding of pepper farming. Visitors often appreciate the quiet ambiance and the personalized attention during the tour and tasting sessions.
picks.whatToOrder: Their fresh green pepper corns, if available seasonally, for a truly unique taste.
picks.insiderTip: They sometimes have a small guesthouse or bungalows for a truly immersive stay. Inquire directly if interested in an overnight experience.
picks.redditQuote: "Secret Garden Pepper Farm was a nice, quiet break. It wasn't as grand as La Plantation, but the guide was super friendly, and it felt very personal. A real hidden gem."

picks.name: Salang Farm
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Salang Farm provides a glimpse into a more traditional and rural pepper farming operation. The tours often highlight the manual labor and community effort involved in cultivating Kampot pepper, offering a rustic and authentic perspective. It’s an eye-opening experience into local agricultural life.
picks.whatToOrder: Support them by purchasing their black pepper, known for its robust flavor from traditional methods.
picks.insiderTip: This farm is a bit further out, so plan your transportation accordingly. A full-day tuk-tuk rental is recommended to combine it with other sights.
picks.redditQuote: "Salang Farm was a deep dive into the real, hardworking side of pepper farming. No frills, just honest work and incredible pepper. Felt very authentic."

picks.name: Traeuy Koh Pepper Farm
picks.whyItMadeTheList: This farm represents a collective effort within the Traeuy Koh community to produce high-quality Kampot pepper. Tours emphasize the cooperative model and the benefits of direct trade for the local families. It’s a great way to learn about the socio-economic impact of Kampot pepper.
picks.whatToOrder: Any of their packaged pepper varieties; your purchase directly supports the community.
picks.insiderTip: This farm is often part of larger cycling tours through the countryside. Consider joining one for a scenic and active way to visit.
picks.redditQuote: "Loved visiting Traeuy Koh. It's not just a farm; it's a community project. The tour gave me a real appreciation for the teamwork involved in growing this amazing spice."

picks.name: Phnom Chhngan Pepper Farm
picks.whyItMadeTheList: This farm is unique for its proximity to the Phnom Chhngan Caves, allowing visitors to combine a pepper tour with cave exploration. The farm tour provides solid insights into pepper cultivation, while the nearby caves offer a natural attraction, making for a diverse half-day trip.
picks.whatToOrder: Their black Kampot pepper, known for its strong aromatic qualities.
picks.insiderTip: Wear comfortable shoes suitable for walking and potentially some light climbing if you plan to explore the caves.
picks.redditQuote: "Combining the pepper farm with the Phnom Chhngan Caves was brilliant. Got to learn about pepper and then explore some cool natural formations. A great combo trip!"

picks.name: Kep Organic Pepper Farm
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Located closer to the coastal town of Kep, this organic farm offers tours focusing on sustainable practices and the specific terroir that gives Kampot pepper its unique flavor. It's a convenient option for those staying in Kep and looking for a quality pepper experience without venturing far into Kampot province.
picks.whatToOrder: Their certified organic white pepper, known for its delicate yet pungent flavor.
picks.insiderTip: Pair your visit with a fresh seafood lunch at the Kep Crab Market, just a short drive away.
picks.redditQuote: "Being based in Kep, this organic pepper farm was super easy to get to. The tour was thorough, and I felt good about buying their organic products. Plus, the views were lovely!"

faq.question: What is Kampot pepper and why is it so famous?
faq.answer: Kampot pepper is a geographical indication (GI) protected spice grown exclusively in Cambodia's Kampot and Kep provinces. Its fame stems from its unique terroir – the rich soil, specific climate, and traditional farming methods – which contribute to its distinct, complex flavor profile and intense aroma, highly prized by chefs worldwide.

faq.question: What are the different colors of Kampot pepper and what do they taste like?
faq.answer: Kampot pepper comes in four main colors, all from the same plant but processed differently: Black (harvested unripe, sun-dried, pungent, strong aroma), Red (fully ripe, sun-dried, fruity, slightly sweet), White (red pepper dehusked, subtle, floral, less heat), and Green (fresh, young berries, often pickled or used raw, herbaceous, bright).

faq.question: Do I need to book a pepper plantation tour in advance?
faq.answer: While many larger plantations like La Plantation welcome walk-ins for their standard tours, booking in advance is highly recommended, especially during peak season or if you have a specific time or language preference. Smaller, family-run farms might require a call ahead to ensure someone is available to guide you.

faq.question: How much does a Kampot pepper plantation tour typically cost?
faq.answer: Most Kampot pepper plantation tours range from $5 to $12 USD per person (approximately 20,000 to 48,000 KHR). Some farms offer free tours with the expectation that visitors will purchase products, while others include tastings or a small gift in the tour price. Transportation to the farm is usually an additional cost.

faq.question: What is the best time of year to visit Kampot pepper plantations?
faq.answer: The harvest season for Kampot pepper is generally from March to May, which is an exciting time to visit as you can see the vines laden with peppercorns and observe the initial stages of processing. However, farms offer tours year-round, as there's always something to learn about the cultivation and history of the spice.

faq.question: Can I buy Kampot pepper directly from the plantations?
faq.answer: Yes, absolutely! Most Kampot pepper plantations have onsite shops where you can purchase various types of Kampot pepper (black, red, white, green), pepper-infused products, and often other local spices or crafts. Buying directly from the farm ensures authenticity and supports the local producers.

methodology: Our selection of Kampot pepper plantation tours was meticulously curated based on extensive research, traveler reviews across platforms like TripAdvisor and Google, and local recommendations. We prioritized farms offering educational tours, high-quality tasting experiences, and sustainable practices, ensuring a rich and authentic visit.
